Student Assistant- Structural Department

Do you want to kick-start your career in one of Denmark’s largest buildings division? Are you passionate about building technology, structures and structural engineering? And are you curious and ambitious? Then join COWI and develop your potential in a unique professional environment!

JOIN OUR STRUCTURES SECTION IN LYNGBY

At COWI Denmark, you will become part of COWI’s Buildings division. We provide consultancy services for all types of buildings and every aspect of the construction process. We take a holistic approach to projects, focusing on functionality, value, building technology, energy optimization and sustainable solutions.

In this position, you will join our Structures department in Lyngby, which consists of more than 50 structural engineers. You will also be part of a larger multidisciplinary department across the Buildings & Industry division. The team has a strong sense of community and includes both experienced and recently graduated engineers, all of whom contribute professional pride and strong collegial relationships. We have a broad and highly skilled nationwide network that promotes knowledge sharing and professional sparring.

As a student assistant, you will become part of our national team and work closely with the section’s specialists, other student assistants and your immediate manager. Our department delivers a wide range of exciting projects, including Airports, Hospital, Pharma, Water treatment plants, Datacenters, several major and minor renovation projects, and many other interesting assignments. You can look forward to working in a strong professional environment with engaging and developmental tasks, which may include:

• Preparing structural documentation acc. to BR18 and SBi 271.

• Contributing to and supporting professional development and knowledge sharing within the department

• Working with older building cases, including obtaining documentation and reviewing structural documentation

• Assisting the departments specialists on projects by carrying out both administrative and calculation tasks

• Helping facilitate courses and meetings designed to develop the department and keep it up to date with the latest knowledge, technologies, methods and regulations in the construction industry

• Helping to strengthen the social community within the department.

• Support department managers with administrative tasks

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that you:

• Are studying engineering within the field of buildings and construction.

• Have knowledge of building technology, structural analysis and structures, including a basic understanding of concrete, steel and timber.

• Have good communication skills in both Danish and English

Do you want to lead ICT management and digital delivery on complex civil infrastructure projects? Can you translate contractual and project-specific ICT requirements into clear governance, practical workflows and successful technical implementation? Are you motivated by bringing clients, project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists together on projects such as bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure? Then this could be the next step in your career.

Lead ICT management from requirements to implementation

As our new ICT expert, you will lead ICT management, digital governance and digital delivery on multidisciplinary civil infrastructure projects. Our work includes bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure, often involving complex interfaces between disciplines, organisations and project phases.

You will advise clients and project organization, translate contractual and project-specific requirements into practical processes and workflows, and drive their technical implementation in collaboration with project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists.

The position is a project-based leadership role and combines professional leadership of the ICT process, leadership of the project’s digital delivery and client-facing advice.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Lead ICT management and digital delivery through relevant project phases, from mobilisation and planning to execution and handover.

• Advise clients and project management on ICT requirements, BIM processes, information management and digital governance.

• Prepare, maintain and implement project-specific ICT documentation based on Molio’s ICT paradigms, contractual requirements and relevant industry standards.

• Translate requirements into clear roles, responsibilities, workflows, digital deliverables and quality-assurance procedures.

• Establish the project’s digital delivery framework, including model and information requirements, naming conventions, exchange procedures, coordination processes and Common Data Environment structures.

• Drive the technical implementation of ICT requirements together with project management, engineering disciplines, BIM coordinators, Digital Design specialists and other technical contributors.

• Facilitate ICT kick-off meetings, workshops and coordination activities, ensuring that agreed processes are understood and applied across the project organisation.

• Manage interfaces with internal and external stakeholders, including clients, project managers, discipline leads, architects, contractors, and international delivery teams.

• Identify opportunities for project-specific automation and digital improvements and coordinate their implementation with the relevant specialists.

• Contribute lessons learned and proven workflows to the continued development of COWI’s ICT management practices.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you enjoy creating structure and direction together with others. You communicate clearly, build trusted relationships and can align stakeholders with different technical backgrounds, priorities and contractual responsibilities.

You are motivated by turning requirements and strategies into solutions that work in practice. You understand that successful ICT management requires robust governance as well as active involvement in project implementation.

On top of that, you will have:

• At least 7 years of relevant experience within ICT management, BIM management, digital project delivery or a comparable field in the engineering and construction industry.

• Practical experience leading ICT management or digital delivery on multidisciplinary projects.

• Strong knowledge of Molio’s ICT paradigms and practical experience applying them on multidisciplinary projects.

• Knowledge of relevant Danish industry standards and contractual frameworks, including YBL18 and YBB19 where applicable

• Knowledge of relevant global Industry standards such as ISO 19650

• Experience translating client and contractual requirements into practical digital processes, workflows and deliverables.

• Experience driving technical implementation, for example through Common Data Environment structures, coordination workflows, quality-control procedures, data exchanges or automated checking processes.

• A strong understanding of BIM processes, information management, digital collaboration and multidisciplinary coordination.

• General knowledge of relevant digital delivery applications such as Revit, Tekla, OpenRoadsDesign

• Experience with Coordination and Common Data Environment platforms, such as Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud), Navisworks; Bentley Infrastructure Cloud and ProjectWise; and Trimble Connect and Quadri—or comparable systems.

• Strong planning, facilitation, communication and stakeholder-management skills.

• Professional proficiency in English and Danish.

You do not need to be a software developer or perform every technical task yourself. However, you must have sufficient technical understanding to define the project’s needs, involve the right specialists, guide implementation and ensure that the resulting solutions are adopted by the project organisation.

Your professional environment

You will become part of Digital Design within Structures and Digital Engineering. We support the delivery of complex civil infrastructure projects, including bridges, tunnels, marine structures and other major infrastructure.

You will work closely with project management, engineering disciplines and digital specialists to establish consistent digital processes across multidisciplinary projects. You will join a collaborative professional environment where knowledge sharing, technical development and practical project value are closely connected.

The role allows you to influence both individual projects and the continued development of our ICT management practices.

Do you have the technical expertise and leadership experience to lead electrical design delivery on large-scale data centre projects?

As Electrical Lead at COWI, you will take a central technical role in some of our largest and most complex data centre projects. You will lead electrical design teams, act as a key technical interface with clients and partners and can shape how COWI develops and delivers electrical design for data centres across the Nordics and internationally. Data centre work experience specifically with hyperscale projects is a requirement for this position. Your work base will be at one of COWI's offices in either Lyngby, Odense, Vejle, Aarhus or Aalborg based on where you live in Denmark.

Grow COWI’s international data centre business

Data centres are a strategic growth area at COWI, and we are continuing to strengthen our capabilities and position in this market. As Electrical Lead, you will combine technical leadership on major projects with significant influence on how we approach electrical design and develop consistent ways of working across our data centre business.

You will work closely with clients, Senior Project Managers, Project Directors, Design Managers and multidisciplinary engineering teams across different project stages. You will work in an English-speaking environment alongside colleagues across the Nordics and the UK.

• Act as the technical electrical lead towards clients, partners and other external stakeholders, translating project requirements into appropriate technical solutions

• Lead electrical design teams on large-scale data centre projects, with overall responsibility for the electrical design delivery.

• Plan and manage the electrical design process, coordinating resources, activities, interfaces and deliverables across project stages and delivery teams.

• Lead the technical development of data centre electrical power systems and technical architecture, covering critical power, MV/LV distribution, UPS, generators, redundancy and resilience, as well as ICC, BMS and ELV systems and their interfaces with other technical disciplines.

• Ensure technical quality and consistency of the electrical design, providing senior technical direction and supporting key design decisions and complex interfaces.

• Contribute to the continued development of COWI’s data centre capabilities, helping shape our technical approaches and ways of working across projects and international delivery teams.

You are comfortable taking technical responsibility in demanding project environments and representing the electrical discipline towards clients and project partners.

You have the technical breadth and engineering judgement to lead the overall electrical design delivery and guide specialists across the wider electrical scope. You communicate clearly, work effectively across disciplines and bring a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to complex engineering challenges.

To be considered for this role, you should have:

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

Our IoT team builds the devices and edge software that connect our customers' production lines to the Factbird platform, from sensors on the line to industrial edge computers running computer vision right next to the machines. We're a small team with broad ownership, and we're hiring an Embedded Platform Engineer to help build and run the platform our edge products stand on.

**This role is onsite in Copenhagen, Denmark. We welcome applications from candidates based in Germany who are open to relocating to Copenhagen.

**

About the Role

As Embedded Platform Engineer, you'll work hands-on across Factbird EDGE, our industrial edge platform, together with the rest of the IoT team: the operating system, the device software, and the vision models that run on it. You'll take ownership of the infrastructure around the devices: provisioning and recovery, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability, the systems that keep our unattended devices reliable, secure, and safely updatable in factories you may never visit.

You'll work in Rust on embedded Linux, with Yocto, AWS IoT Greengrass, GStreamer and ONNX Runtime at the core, alongside our Cloud and DevOps engineers and the people building our AI capabilities. Part of the job is shaping the role with the team as our edge products grow.

You'll thrive here if you like working across a system end to end, from the bootloader to the cloud connection, and if you'd rather fix the root cause in the build than patch around it on the device.

What you'll do

Embedded Linux & the EDGE platform

• Develop our Yocto-based Linux distribution: layers, BSPs, kernel configuration, and reproducible builds

• Build and maintain the Rust components that run on our edge devices

• Bring up new hardware platforms, debug on target, and keep the platform secure and maintainable over a long device lifetime

• Keep our CI and on-hardware testing healthy, so changes reach devices with confidence

Edge inference & vision

• Work with our ML and vision engineers on the device side of our computer vision capabilities: camera pipelines, video streaming, and model inference that runs efficiently on industrial hardware

• Share ownership with our ML engineers of how trained models move from our model pipeline onto devices and how they perform there: packaging, rollout, rollback, and drift monitoring

• Help bring new edge runtimes for vision workloads from development into production

Fleet infrastructure & ownership

• Own device provisioning, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability

• Make deployments to devices in the field safe and boring: staged rollouts, health checks, and recovery paths

• Help diagnose issues on devices at customer sites, working with Support, Product, and Cloud to turn them into lasting fixes

• Share knowledge in both directions: learn the parts of the platform others built, and make sure what you build doesn't live only in your head

**What we're looking for

**

We're looking for an engineer who has shipped embedded Linux into production and lived with it afterwards: someone who has debugged a device they couldn't touch, and who wants real responsibility rather than a ticket queue.

You work independently, but you don't work alone. You can take a loosely defined problem and move it forward without daily direction, and you pull others in early, because on a small team the best fix is one more than one person understands. You're disciplined where it matters, in releases and rollouts, and curious where it pays off, in vision and new hardware.

You don't need everything below. Yocto is the core. Rust matters, but strong C/C++ engineers who have started with Rust are welcome too. The rest you can grow into with us.

**

The ideal background**

• Hands-on experience shipping embedded Linux to production, including Yocto: layers, BSPs and images you've built and maintained yourself, not just consumed

• Strong systems programming in Rust, or deep C/C++ experience on embedded Linux and real exposure to Rust that you want to build on

• An advantage if you have worked with AWS IoT Core or Greengrass, video pipelines or ML inference on edge hardware, or in industrial settings where devices run unattended for years

• A solid grasp of embedded security and update mechanisms: signed images, A/B or similar update schemes, and secure device provisioning

• You can explain a technical trade-off clearly, whether you're talking to another engineer, Support or a customer, and you do it in fluent English

• We welcome applications from people eager to move to Denmark, as long as you already have the legal right to live and work here.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We'd love to hear from you

**

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at **crva@factbird.com

Can you lead the commercial and sourcing dimensions of complex transformation projects, navigating multiple priorities and demanding stakeholder environments? Danske Bank's Procurement team is looking for a Senior Commercial & Sourcing Specialist to shape and deliver commercially sound outcomes on strategically significant initiatives. You will work at the centre of our Forward'28 strategy, with real scope to make your mark.

What you will be doing

You will join a professional, collegial team within Procurement & Premises, working on initiatives spanning outsourcing, technology sourcing, BPO, partnerships and M&A. Collaborating closely with procurement managers, business leaders, legal and specialist functions, you will bring structure and sound judgement to complex commercial workstreams within major transformation programmes. The team combines high professional standards with an open, supportive atmosphere where good work is noticed.

More specifically, you will:

• Translate business requirements into clear commercial positions and contractual provisions with legal teams

• Analyse pricing, financial models and total cost of ownership to weigh cost, value and risk

• Shape and lead high-stakes supplier negotiations involving complex commercial models and contractual dependencies

• Lead commercial workstreams across programmes with multiple functions, suppliers and interdependent decisions

• Present clear recommendations, trade-offs and decisions to senior stakeholders across relevant forums

About you

• At least 10 years of experience in strategic procurement, sourcing, contract management or commercial finance

• Demonstrable track record of leading commercial delivery within complex projects and programmes

• Ability to scrutinise complex agreements and translate negotiated intentions into clear contractual obligations

• Comfortable working with detailed financial models, assessing pricing logic and weighing cost, value and risk

• Experience leading demanding supplier negotiations and securing robust agreements

• Understanding of digital outsourcing, technology sourcing and BPO commercial models

• Strong communicator in English, both verbally and in writing, with the ability to present clearly to senior decision-makers

If your background is in commercial finance, legal or deal advisory rather than procurement directly, we welcome your application. What matters most is your track record of leading commercial outcomes in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

What we offer you

This role offers meaningful involvement in significant commercial decisions across a varied portfolio of complex group-wide projects. You will be based in Copenhagen with the option to work from home a couple of days each week. Benefits include a canteen, health insurance, pension and six weeks of holiday per year, within a team that takes the work seriously and enjoys doing it together.

Are you ready for the next step?

Apply with your CV and a short example of a complex sourcing or transformation initiative in which you held a leading commercial role. Describe what made it complex, how you navigated competing stakeholder priorities and what you delivered. If you have any questions before applying, please contact hiring manager Magnus Jacobsen at magnus.jacobsen@danskebank.dk.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 25 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Simulation Engineer specializing in finite element analysis (FEA) to join our team in Hillerød and support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

Your new role

As our Senior Simulation Engineer, you will take technical ownership of structural simulation activities, helping teams develop reliable products and make informed design decisions. You will work across the product lifecycle, from evaluating early design concepts to supporting validation, product improvements and failure investigations.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Lead finite element analyses: Independently plan and execute structural simulations, selecting appropriate methods to assess performance, durability and safety under realistic loading conditions.

• Build reliable simulation models: Translate engineering requirements and CAD designs into robust models, defining geometry, meshes, material behavior, contacts and boundary conditions. Verify model quality through convergence and sensitivity studies.

• Support design optimization: Collaborate with design and mechanical engineers to improve product performance, material selection and cost. Provide practical recommendations and technical input during design reviews.

• Validate simulations against physical tests: Work with physical test and define validation activities, correlate simulation results with experimental data, assess uncertainty and refine models based on findings.

• Support product development and failure investigations: Contribute structural analysis expertise to cross-functional teams working on new products, product maintenance, validation and root cause analysis.

• Communicate findings clearly: Prepare reports and presentations that explain analysis methods, assumptions, results and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Advance simulation practices and develop colleagues: Improve simulation methods, workflows and standards, contribute to the structural simulation strategy, and mentor junior engineers and interns.

Your new department

You will join Drug Delivery Innovation (DDI), a new area within Novo Nordisk’s global organization, based in Hillerød.

Our team comprises 14 colleagues across three specialist groups: Structural Simulation, Molding Simulation and Material Science. We work closely together and collaborate with stakeholders across Novo Nordisk, combining expertise in simulation and materials to support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

Practical experience in manual and automated testing (Python or similar), test design, debugging and defect investigation.

• 
Experience with Git, code review, CI/CD, reusable test automation components and reproducible data analysis.

•

• 
An understanding of risk-based validation and data integrity, and the ability to judge whether test evidence supports a system’s intended use.

•

• 
Motivation to build expertise in GCP-regulated clinical data science, AI evaluation and emerging data modalities.

What you’ll do

Design, execute and document manual tests (for example via the user interface) and automated tests in Python or similar, producing reproducible evidence that workflows and supporting IT/AI systems perform as intended.

Project Manager – Operations

Location: Lyngby, Denmark

Do you have a proven track record of turning complex operational challenges into tangible results? Are you motivated by getting close to manufacturing operations, analysing performance and working with teams to implement improvements that make a measurable difference?

We are looking for a Project Manager who combines strong analytical and problem-solving capability with the drive, resilience and hands-on approach required to deliver outcomes in complex manufacturing environments.

If you enjoy taking ownership, solving difficult problems and seeing your work translate into improved operational performance, this could be your next career move.

The position

As a Project Manager, you will work as part of our internal operations and manufacturing consulting team, delivering complex improvement, operational readiness and ramp up projects across our global manufacturing network.

This is not a traditional PMO or project coordination role.

You will be expected to get close to the operation, spend time on the shop floor, understand what is really happening within the production environment and use data and structured problem-solving to identify opportunities for improvement.

More importantly, your responsibility does not end when the solution has been identified. You will work alongside manufacturing teams and stakeholders to turn recommendations into actions and deliver tangible operational outcomes.

Our projects are typically intensive assignments, with project teams substantially dedicated to one project at a time. Assignments will often run for six to twelve months and can sometimes continue for longer.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Taking ownership of project workstreams and operational improvement initiatives from diagnosis through to implementation and delivery.

• Driving operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, helping manufacturing operations achieve stable target performance.

• Working directly with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams to understand operational challenges and identify bottlenecks, losses and improvement opportunities.

• Analysing operational performance data and developing capacity models, process maps and improvement scenarios.

• Translating complex analysis into clear recommendations, practical implementation roadmaps and measurable actions.

• Driving implementation and following improvements through to tangible operational outcomes.

• Working with production teams to establish sustainable changes in performance and ways of working.

• Collaborating with stakeholders across manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain and site leadership.

• Influencing stakeholders and maintaining momentum when implementation is challenging or priorities change.

• Communicating progress, risks, recommendations and outcomes clearly to relevant stakeholders and project leadership.

This is a hands on role. You should be comfortable moving between analytical problem-solving and the realities of implementation on the manufacturing shop floor.

The position is based in Lyngby, Denmark, and requires flexibility for up to 50% global travel.

Travel requirements will depend on project assignment and may change throughout a project. The ability and willingness to travel flexibly according to business and project requirements is therefore an essential requirement of the position.

Qualifications

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate a proven track record of delivering outcomes, rather than simply participating in projects.

You combine strong intellectual and analytical capability with the practical judgement, resilience and persistence required to turn ideas into results.

To succeed in this role, you:

• Hold a relevant degree in engineering, science, business administration, economics or another relevant discipline.

• Have relevant professional experience within areas such as manufacturing, operational excellence, operations consulting, engineering, supply chain, procurement or complex cross-functional project work.

• Can demonstrate a proven track record of taking ownership and delivering tangible outcomes through projects, operational improvements or complex cross-functional initiatives.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and structured problem-solving capability.

• Are comfortable personally analysing operational data and using it to identify performance gaps, bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.

• Can translate analysis into practical recommendations and then follow those recommendations through implementation.

• Are comfortable working hands-on with manufacturing sites and shop-floor teams.

• Can operate effectively in complex and ambiguous environments where the solution may not initially be obvious.

• Demonstrate strong stakeholder management, collaboration and communication skills.

• Have the resilience and persistence to continue driving change when implementation is difficult or initial solutions do not deliver the expected results.

• Are professionally proficient in English.

• Are able and willing to travel globally for up to 50% of your time according to project requirements.

Relevant experience from operations or management consulting can be particularly valuable, including experience gained within operational practices or projects.

We are also interested in candidates from complex manufacturing environments such as pharmaceuticals, automotive, aerospace and FMCG, particularly where you have worked with operational improvement, production ramp-up, manufacturing performance or Lean ways of working.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing, GMP and validation experience are advantageous but are not essential.

Experience working within a Lean manufacturing environment can also be beneficial. Formal Lean certification is not required.

Likewise, formal project management qualifications such as PMP or PRINCE2 are not a requirement. We place greater emphasis on your demonstrated ability to structure problems, work with people, take ownership and deliver measurable outcomes.

About the department

You will join Drug Product Manufacturing Excellence, a global unit responsible for driving performance improvements, operational readiness and transformation across Novo's manufacturing network.

The team operates as an internal operations and manufacturing consultancy, supporting our manufacturing organisation with complex operational challenges.

Our colleagues bring diverse professional backgrounds, including operations and management consulting, Novo manufacturing and support functions, and industries such as automotive, aerospace and FMCG.

What brings the team together is the ability to combine analytical problem-solving with hands-on implementation.

Our projects can include operational readiness and ramp-up of new production lines, improving capacity and performance within existing operations and solving complex cross-functional manufacturing challenges.

Rather than managing several projects simultaneously, our project teams are typically substantially dedicated to one assignment, allowing them to work closely with the operation and remain involved from diagnosis through to implementation.

As a Project Manager, you will have meaningful ownership within these assignments and will be expected to demonstrate that your work ultimately translates into operational outcomes.

The role provides significant exposure to different manufacturing environments, functions and senior stakeholders across our global organisation and offers opportunities to progress towards increasingly complex project and leadership responsibilities.

Working at Novo

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What you’ll bring

You thrive where commercial business development, consumer behaviour and financial decision making meet. You can build something new, influence without formal authority and turn complexity into action.

• A master’s degree in economics, business administration, finance or an equivalent field.

• Significant experience in commercial finance, business development, M&A finance, financial system change projects or customer profitability, including cross-country, regional or global exposure.

• Strong financial modelling and data interpretation skills.

• Practical experience in pricing, negotiation, customer profitability and stakeholder management in a large organisation.

• Experience bringing structure to new business areas, setting clear priorities and steering the business through influence and relationships.

• The ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations and to build new capabilities, standards and frameworks from the ground up.

• Fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience from consumer health companies, including private healthcare organisations.

• Additional languages.

You will be the finance partner who helps Region Europe and Canada decide where to invest in online partnerships and consumer initiatives, and who shows what those investments deliver.

• Create the framework and shape commercial partnership priorities through sound financial modelling, working with business partners to assess partnership opportunities and consumer investment initiatives.

• Develop and deliver a business case methodology across European markets, so investment decisions are prudent, comparable and grounded in facts as part of the business rhythm.

• Establish an end-to-end view of customer and partner profit and loss, including system tracking and performance updates that follow return on investment.

• Deliver complex cross-functional change projects with Business Development, Finance, Legal, Supply Chain and Commercial Strategy to enable online sales in new European markets.

• Improve data definitions, ownership, quality and comparability of online sales channels across markets.

You will build bridges between these functions, so every investment decision rests on evidence and aims to maximise patient reach. The role is based in Ørestad, Copenhagen, Denmark.

You will shape a new area from the start, with the trust to set direction and the visibility to influence decisions across European markets. Working with colleagues from finance, commercial, legal and supply chain, you will broaden your perspective across the value chain and build new skills through practical, cross-functional experience.
